subject.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw Tool Lifecycle / Gateway Recovery Field Report

question: For post-tool continuation failures with side effects, should OpenClaw prioritize automatic session-survival/resume semantics, durable quarantine/receipt diagnostics, or keep the current fail-closed warning until a narrower provider-specific root cause is proven?
rationale: The current code intentionally fails closed for replay-unsafe post-tool attempts, and choosing a safe recovery contract affects session state, retry policy, transcript repair, and user-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Define session-survival contract
options.body: Specify when the runner may resume from persisted current-turn state and when it must quarantine an unsafe attempt, then implement the narrow recovery path with tests and live proof.

options.title: Track under narrower issues
options.body: Treat this report as field evidence for the existing replay-unsafe and quarantine trackers while keeping implementation focused on those narrower root causes.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the current warning behavior until a maintainer or reporter captures a current-main Ollama/Gemma run with logs, transcript, and provider payloads.

recommendation.title: Define session-survival contract
recommendation.body: Specify when the runner may resume from persisted current-turn state and when it must quarantine an unsafe attempt, then implement the narrow recovery path with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This account owns the most recent merged work on terminal-state selection, replay provenance, and post-tool incomplete-turn behavior in the implicated runner path.
